title: note: doc.importFile is a stub — not supported in browser context
description:
In packages/authoring-ui/src/jsfl/runtime.ts, `doc.importFile(fileURL, importToLibrary)` is a stub that only logs a console warning:

```ts
importFile(_fileURL: string, _importToLibrary?: boolean): void {
  console.warn('doc.importFile: not supported in browser context');
}
```

**Impact:** Any JSFL script that calls `fl.getDocumentDOM().importFile(url)` to import bitmaps, sounds, or other assets into the document will silently do nothing. This affects automated workflows and JSFL-driven authoring scripts.

**Scope for a real implementation:** For the browser/Electron context, the implementation would need to:
1. Accept a file URL or path
2. Load the file (bitmap/sound/video) as binary data
3. Add it to the document library as the appropriate item type (BitmapItem/SoundItem/etc.)

This is a known limitation. If JSFL-driven asset import is needed for the capstone or agent workflows, this needs to be implemented.

**Priority:** Low unless a specific workflow needs it; file as a known gap.
